reason: The invariant the equivalence rests on (X entering subtract_delta is &40-&7F, or 0 for a never-plotted mover) is false, and the two codes differ for a result in &80-&BF. movers_screen_address_high starts &00 (src/game.6502:842). No add_new_movers path writes it, so a mover in a fresh slot keeps 0 until the edge calculation runs. If that mover moves left (move_mover_left -> subtract_delta, Y=0, low byte < 8 borrows), it gets &00-&00-1 = &FF, kept by both codes. If it then moves right, add_delta_to_screen_address_in_AX gives &FF+0 with N set, so wrap_add_delta_g4566 subtracts &40 and leaves &BF (or &FE -> &BE). If it moves left again, subtract gives &BF/&BE: the original's CMP #&40/BCS keeps &BF/&BE, but ORA #&40 gives &FF/&FE. That is a different movers_screen_address_high (stored at 2979 via mover_screen_address_high). The renderer reads it (record_live/world_of_address, draw's dm_scr_hi, the record compare at render.6502:2368) and so do projectiles fired from that mover (4203-4227). This is state the passlock oracle compares, so the change is not equivalent on every path. The flags are fine: C differs only in the wrap and inactive cases, and every continuation writes C before reading it (CPY/CPX/SEC/ASL; start_column's PLP carries it on to scroll_screen_left, then ASL or SEC). V is the same. The SKIP 4 keeps subtract_Y_rows and the self-modified JSR's page in place. But the value range is wrong, so it is refuted.
